summary: Installed all four tiers of the conflict-response ladder (auto-sequence, bounded retry, warn, ask) across task-lock.sh, command-gate-in.sh, the three plain multi-task commands, and durable docs. All 8 phases complete; an 11-case isolated-temp-root suite proves all four tiers plus non-convergence-as-partial. Phase 8 closed COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS for expected deploy-tree drift (source-store-only edits; regeneration is manual-only) and two unrelated pre-existing literature-extension pycache findings.
decisions_made: Retry loop wraps cmd_acquire from the outside, never edits its body: cmd_acquire holds the process-global specs/.scope-lock mutex for its entire body via a RETURN trap, so a retry inside it would hold that mutex across the wait window and be reclaimed by a competing waiter after SCOPE_MUTEX_STALE_SEC. acquire-retry calls the full, unmodified cmd_acquire fresh per attempt instead.

orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's collision predicate is a state.json STATUS check, not a lock check, so the plain multi-task Tier-1 second pass genuinely converges only once the pass-1 winner reaches a terminal status -- natural for /implement, not for /research or /plan. This is the expected non-convergence case the plan's Risks table anticipated, not a defect.
Tier 4 (ask) is gated on orchestrator_mode and deliberately not wired into /orchestrate, /revise, or /task -- a recorded decision, not an omission.
